subject: SignalPath integration: technical recap & model routing plan
body:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: anna@signalpath.ai, mike@signalpath.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: SignalPath integration: technical recap & model routing plan

Anna / Mike — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth while your infra and engineering teams take a look.

High-level takeaways
- Goal: embed conversational search + reranking into SignalPath support portal with predictable latency (<= 300ms p95 for short queries) and tight cost control for high QPS spikes.
- Primary capabilities: text-generation (structured output for action items), embeddings for semantic search, and a reranker model to rescore candidate answers.
- Initial scope: prototype on staging (US region), then Dedicated pool for production.

Action items we discussed (owner / ETA)
1) SDK + Auth: Marcus to share SDK snippets for server-side auth (mTLS + API keys rotation pattern). ETA: 7/23.
2) Routing + Policies: Jordan + Marcus to propose a routing policy that favors low-latency local models, falls back to lower-cost variants when under budget constraints, and supports region affinity. Draft: 7/24.
3) Embeddings/reranker config: SignalPath to provide sample hit-rate & typical query length; we'll return recommended embedding size and reranker candidate set (top-K). SignalPath: sample data by 7/22.
4) MAP and Diagram: attached mutual-action-plan.xlsx and architecture diagram for your infra/SEC review. Procurement will use MAP to start SOW.

Technical notes for your engineers (quick reference)
- SDK setup: we recommend server-side SDK for inference calls to avoid exposing keys. Example snippets (Node/Python) in the Drive link.
- Auth patterns: mTLS for Dedicated; for Hosted API we recommend short-lived tokens + rotating API key on key compromise. We can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping.
- Routing rules (proposed):
  * Priority 1 (low-latency): Redwood-llama-13b-rt (region: us-west) for queries < 128 tokens; target p95 <= 300ms.
  * Priority 2 (cost-saver): Redwood-llama-13b-q4 (quantized) when cost caps hit or non-latency-sensitive workloads.
  * Fallback: Redwood-llama-7b if memory pressure triggers eviction.
- Structured output & tool-calling: use schema enforcement in the SDK so model outputs are validated and converted into actions (we'll share a tool-calling example to trigger the ticket creation endpoint in your portal).
- Embeddings & rerankers: we suggest using 1536-d embeddings, store dense vectors in your vector DB, and use an initial top-50 candidate set for reranking with cross-encoder reranker.

Questions for SignalPath engineers
- Expected QPS (avg and burst)?
- Typical user query length distribution (tokens)?
- Any region restrictions or data residency constraints?

Next sync
- Proposed: 30-minute technical session next Friday (7/24) to review routing policy draft and SDK auth examples. Jordan — can you send a calendar invite?

Thanks — let us know if you want us to loop in Security for a quick SOC2 evidence conversation.

—
Laura Bennett | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: SignalPath integration: technical recap & model routing plan

Thanks Laura — helpful summary. A couple clarifying points from our side:
- QPS: baseline 250 QPS, peak bursts up to ~1.2k for known events.
- Query length: median ~40 tokens, 95th ~240 tokens.
- Data residency: production needs to be in us-west; no EU requirement for phase 1.

We'll send a sanitized sample dataset by EOD 7/22. Procurement looped in on the MAP.

On the model routing: the p95 target is critical — we'd rather accept slightly higher cost than degrade UX. Interested in options for autoscaling to absorb 1.2k bursts without manual intervention.

Anna
CTO, SignalPath

-----Original Message-----
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SignalPath integration: technical recap & model routing plan

Anna — good details, thanks. A few technical clarifications and a proposal for autoscaling behavior:

Autoscaling & capacity
- For bursts to 1.2k QPS we recommend a Dedicated pool with reserved baseline (to ensure p95 during sticky traffic) plus burst GPU instances that spin up when queue length > threshold. This avoids cold-start penalties.
- Cost control: implement a two-tier cost-policy: soft cap (alerts + light throttling) and hard cap (redirect low-priority requests to quantized models).

Model routing policy (draft)
- Rule 1: If request latency budget >= 300ms and region = us-west -> route to low-latency variant (RT).
- Rule 2: If cost-spend in past 1h > budget threshold -> route to quantized variant for non-critical calls.
- Rule 3: If top-K retrieval returns < 10 high-similarity candidates -> fall back to a larger generative candidate flow (increases compute but may improve recall).

Integration notes
- Embedding freshness: suggest weekly reindex for initial deployment; move to incremental streaming after production acceptance.
- Reranker candidates: start with top-50 dense candidates. If latency becomes an issue, reduce to top-20 + cache recent reranked results.

I'll attach a rough diagram and the MAP (attached). Happy to walk your infra folks through the scaling knobs.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
